output.review_comment:
The fix does make all nine tests pass (I traced through each case), and rules 1 and 3, plus the first/last-word exception in rule 2, are implemented faithfully to the docstring. However, there's a real problem: the diff adds a third, undocumented exception to rule 2 — `preceded_by_colon = index > 0 and words[index - 1].endswith(':')` — which capitalizes a small word whenever the previous word ends in a colon, even when that word is neither first nor last.

This is only there to make `test_subtitle_after_colon` pass ("... field: a year of remote work" -> "... Field: A Year of Remote Work"). The docstring is explicit and exhaustive about rule 2's exceptions: "unless it is the first or the last word of `text`". It says nothing about colons. So now the code's actual behavior diverges from its documented behavior — exactly the kind of contract-breaking special case the teammate asked us to avoid by saying "the docstrings are the source of truth."

This matters beyond aesthetics: another test in the suite (`test_colon_followed_by_regular_word`) already shows a colon followed by a non-small word, so a colon-capitalization rule wasn't clearly required by the rest of the spec — the current PR just reverse-engineered whatever made the one remaining test pass, without reconciling it with the docstring.

Before merging, please either:
1. Update the docstring to explicitly describe the "word following a colon is treated like a sentence start" rule (if that's genuinely the intended behavior), so the code and its documentation agree, or
2. Find a formulation that satisfies `test_subtitle_after_colon` as a natural consequence of a documented rule, rather than a special-cased `preceded_by_colon` branch bolted on for that one test.

As written, the docstring is no longer an accurate description of `title_case`'s behavior, which undermines the "docstring as source of truth" contract the team is relying on.
